name: Turtle soup (stop run)
source: 2016 Mentorship: Market Maker Traps (False Flags, False Breakouts), Liquidity Pools, Reinforcing Liquidity Concepts
summary: Price runs the stops above an old high (or below an old low) and fails to continue. Trade the reversal back into the range, against the breakout traders.
steps: Mark obvious liquidity: old highs and lows, equal highs and equal lows.
Prefer runs AGAINST your higher-timeframe bias (e.g. in a bullish market, a run below an old low).
Wait for price to trade through the level, ideally in a killzone.
Look for failure: price closes back inside the range and displaces away from the extreme.
Enter on the return into the range, or at the order block / FVG the reversal leaves.
entry: After price closes back inside the old high/low, at the PD array left by the reversal.
stop: A few pips beyond the extreme of the stop run.
target: The opposite side of the range or the next obvious liquidity.
invalidation: Price accepts beyond the level (closes and holds there) instead of failing.
checklist: The level is obvious liquidity (old high/low or equal highs/lows)
The run is against the higher-timeframe bias
Price traded through the level and closed back inside
A displacement away from the extreme followed
It's inside the London or New York killzone
Stop is beyond the run's extreme; reward at least 2:1
